rows.question: Some websites put a 'checking your browser' wall in front of their feeds. What decides that a 403 response is one of those walls rather than an ordinary access-denied error?
How does the app work out whether a downloaded document is RSS, Atom (and which Atom version), RDF or JSON Feed before it picks a parser?
During a feed refresh, if fetching the full article from the original website is enabled and it succeeds, are the block and keep rules applied again to the fetched content?
Where do article links get stripped of the marketing and click-tracking junk that newsletters and social networks append to the query string?
How does feed discovery guess feed addresses for a website whose pages don't link to any feed, and how does it avoid suggesting addresses that just bounce back to the homepage?
When the scheduler adapts to how often each RSS source publishes, how is the waiting time until that source gets polled again calculated?
What limits how many feeds hosted on the same website get put into a single background refresh batch?
When old articles get purged automatically, which ones are spared, for example ones I bookmarked or shared publicly?
Where is it worked out how often a feed tends to publish, using the spacing between its articles from the last seven days, so the adaptive refresh schedule has a number to use?
What happens when a client calls the REST API with a username and password while local password login has been disabled in the configuration?
Where does the REST API let an external tool add a single article to one of the user's existing feeds, and what read status does the article get when the caller doesn't specify one?
What happens when someone requests a picture through the built-in image proxy using a link whose signature doesn't match the encoded image address?
How does signing in through a reverse proxy that passes the username in an HTTP header work for the web UI, and what happens if that user doesn't have an account yet?
What happens when a form is submitted to the web interface without a valid anti-forgery token, and why does the login page get different treatment?
Where are newly found articles sent out to chat and notification services such as Matrix, Discord, Slack or ntfy after a feed refresh?
How can the server receiving outgoing webhook calls verify that a request really came from this app?
When the app is deployed behind nginx or another proxy, where is the visitor's own address extracted from the forwarded request headers, and which header is preferred?
Who is allowed to read the Prometheus monitoring stats, and how do the optional username and password interact with the network allowlist?
Which characters are allowed in a username when a new account is created with a password?
Which offset and limit values cause the REST API's entry listing to reject the request as invalid?
Which conflicting or half-configured settings stop the app from starting, for example turning off local login without providing any other way to sign in?
Which spellings are accepted for on/off configuration options, and what happens when a value isn't one of them?
What happens to refresh jobs that are still waiting to be handed to the background workers once the application begins shutting down?
Where is the periodic housekeeping that removes stale login sessions, old articles and unused feed icons carried out?
How does the Google Reader-compatible API cope with client apps that send article IDs in different formats?
How does the Fever-compatible API check who is calling it?
When someone signs in through a generic OpenID Connect provider, which piece of identity information from the provider ends up as the account name, and what happens if none of it is filled in?
Where does the translation code choose between the singular and the various plural wordings of a message for languages such as Russian, Polish or Arabic?
How are database schema upgrades applied, and what happens if one upgrade step fails partway through?
Where are human-friendly relative dates like 'yesterday' or '3 weeks ago' worked out for the web pages?
What happens to a website's favicon after it is downloaded if the image is very large, say thousands of pixels wide? Is it scaled down, kept as is, or thrown away?
Which kinds of IP addresses count as internal and off-limits for outgoing requests? Does carrier-grade NAT address space count?
Say a feed has its own proxy, the application also has a global proxy, and a list of rotating proxies is configured. Which proxy does the feed download actually go through?
How does the web server pick a compression method from the client's Accept-Encoding header, and what happens if the client explicitly refuses uncompressed responses?
Before estimating how long an article takes to read, how does the app tell that the text is mostly written in an East Asian script such as Chinese, Japanese or Korean?
How are date-based entry filter rules evaluated, such as dropping posts dated in the future, before or after a given day, between two dates, or older than some number of days?
How does the article HTML cleanup spot the invisible web beacons that sites embed to find out when someone has opened a post?
When a user starts signing in through Google or an OpenID Connect provider, where are the anti-forgery state value and the PKCE challenge generated?
What happens when a Google Reader-compatible app sends one request that marks an article both read and kept unread, or both adds and removes its star?

When several listen addresses are configured, how does the server decide which ones serve plain HTTP, TLS from certificate files, automatic Let's Encrypt certificates, a Unix socket, or a systemd-activated socket?
When a very long article is saved, how is its text shortened for the full-text search index without splitting a multi-byte UTF-8 character?
Some image hosts block pictures that are hotlinked from other websites. How does the app decide which site to pretend the request came from when it fetches those images through its proxy?
I turned on marking articles as read when I open them, but podcast episodes stay unread after I open them. What decides that?
Which pages of the web interface can be opened without being logged in, instead of redirecting to the login screen?
When I save an article to Pinboard and that link is already bookmarked there, does the app overwrite the existing bookmark?
